subject: POC: network handoff + latency & streaming SLOs for private deployment
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Anna Zhao <anna.zhao@finlogic.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC: network handoff + latency & streaming SLOs for private deployment

Thanks again for the call today, Anna — really useful alignment. Summary below so we have a single reference for the POC handoff and next steps. I copied Marcus and Priyom so engineering can start scoping the test plan.

Key takeaways (agreed):
- Target SLOs for POC: p99 generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token responses (sync); streaming tail latency (time to first token) p99 <= 300ms with concurrency target 50 active streams.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline for initial PoC is sustained 50 concurrent streams, peak bursts to 120 concurrent connections for short windows (<= 2 min).
- Network path: VPN peering via your AWS Direct Connect to our VPC; expected egress bandwidth >= 300 Mbps; packet loss budget < 0.1% across the path.
- Internal hop budget: max 3ms across customer VPC -> edge ingress -> serving cluster (we suggested <3ms mean per-hop to meet p99 goals).
- Fallback policy: if direct peering cannot meet tail latencies we will fall back to a hosted-compatible model variant (quantized) with slightly higher nominal latency — discussed as a contingency only.

Requested artifacts from FinLogic (please attach in reply):
1) Network diagram (CIDR ranges, AZs, Direct Connect VIF details, firewall ACLs).
2) ASN and peering contact details + expected maintenance windows.
3) Any traffic shaping or egress proxy we should know about.

We attached a quick SLO table (slo-table.csv) with the measurement points we'll collect (p50/p90/p95/p99, jitter, retransmits). For the PoC we plan to run both synthetic and application-driven tests:
- Synthetic: iperf/httpload for baseline throughput and packet-loss; TCP/UDP checks.
- Application streaming: Redwood harness (we'll provide a small client) to reproduce streaming connection patterns (chunk sizes, keepalive behavior).

Proposed PoC timeline:
- Fri 2028-04-14: exchange test IPs + firewall rules
- Mon 2028-04-17 to Wed 2028-04-19: active testing window (we will run repeated streaming runs and collect traces)
- Thu 2028-04-20: results review and first-pass regression analysis

Next steps (action owners):
- Anna: share network topology PDF, peering contact, and CIDR list (by EOD 4/12).
- FinLogic devops: open port/ACL for the test IPs we provide.
- Marcus (Redwood): prepare iperf endpoints and baseline throughput test plan.
- Priyom (Redwood): instrument SLO dashboards and define metric tags for the PoC.

Happy to jump on a quick 15-minute sync tomorrow if you want to walk through the topology.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0198

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the clear recap. Attached our internal network diagram (finlogic-network-topology.pdf) — it includes Direct Connect VIF IDs, the transit gateway mapping, and the firewall clusters. A couple of quick clarifications from DevOps:

1) For streaming, what chunk size does the Redwood harness use by default? Our app currently sends 256-byte chunks; will that exaggerate tail latency compared to 1KB chunks?
2) Can Redwood run iperf from your side to our public test IPs, or would you prefer we initiate tests to your endpoints?
3) Our security team asks whether TLS termination is expected at the peering edge or at the serving cluster — we can mirror either but need to know for load balancer rules.

We can provision the CIDRs listed on pg 2 of the PDF. We'll aim to have peering contact info and the formal ACLs by tomorrow EOD (4/12).

Anna Zhao
Senior Platform Engineer | FinLogic
anna.zhao@finlogic.com | +1 617 555 0122

- Priyom: define the SLO instrumentation we need on the Redwood side for the PoC. We'd like span-level traces for first-byte and last-byte, and a label for connection-type (peered vs fallback). Also propose a dashboard layout (we can reuse INF-5023 board).
- Security/ops: expect to request ephemeral test IPs and a temporary firewall rule window 04/17-04/19.

I'll compile the test IPs and share the poctest-instructions.txt tonight. Aim to have the iperf endpoints up by Friday.

Thanks,
Olga

Hi Anna — Marcus here (in infra). Thanks for the topology PDF, that helps. Quick answers:

1) Redwood harness defaults to ~1KB chunks for streaming (we generally see fewer per-request round trips). If your client is sending 256B chunks we recommend testing both patterns; smaller chunks can push more frequent network I/O and increase tail latency. We'll include both 256B and 1KB runs in the PoC.

2) We can initiate iperf from our side to the public test IPs — please confirm the public test IPs and allowed protocol/ports. We'll also run reverse tests to help detect asymmetric routing issues.

3) For lowest end-to-end latency we prefer TLS to terminate at the serving cluster (end-to-end TLS) with TCP passthrough at the peering edge; if your security team needs TLS at the edge we can adapt, but please note it may add ~5-10ms depending on LB setup.

Proposed test slots (PST):
- Tue 04/17 09:00-12:00 (baseline runs: sustained 50 streams + handshake tests)
- Wed 04/18 13:00-17:00 (burst tests + streaming trials with 256B/1KB chunks)

If those work for you we'll prepare the test harness and send poctest-instructions.txt with ephemeral IPs and expected firewall rule entries.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
